name: Bulbospinal Muscular Atrophy
aliases: X-linked Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy

ethnicAssociations: Higher prevalence reported in populations of European and Japanese descent

criteria.description: Presence of expanded CAG trinucleotide repeat in the androgen receptor (AR) gene
Clinical evidence of lower motor neuron degeneration including muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly in bulbar and limb muscles
Mild sensory neuropathy demonstrated by nerve conduction studies
X-linked inheritance pattern with affected male relatives

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of expanded CAG repeat in AR gene plus clinical signs of lower motor neuron involvement including bulbar dysfunction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is confirmatory; electrophysiological studies support diagnosis

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic involuntary muscle twitching of the tongue

searchTerms: worsening weakness of muscles controlling speech and swallowing
difficulty with facial and throat muscles

pathognomonic.notes: Breast tissue enlargement in affected males due to androgen receptor dysfunction

common.notes: Predominantly proximal and distal muscles of the limbs
searchTerms: weak and shrinking arm or leg muscles
loss of muscle strength and size

common.notes: Mild sensory loss or abnormal sensations in distal limbs
searchTerms: nerve pain in hands and feet

common.notes: Generalized tiredness related to muscle weakness

occasional.notes: Postural or action tremor in upper limbs
Difficulty swallowing due to bulbar muscle involvement
Subtle executive dysfunction reported in some cases

rare.notes: Including diabetes mellitus or testicular dysfunction
searchTerms: hormone imbalances other than breast enlargement

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase (mild to moderate elevation)
Hormonal abnormalities including elevated estradiol and reduced testosterone
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective muscle atrophy
Brain MRI typically normal or nonspecific
genetic: Expanded CAG trinucleotide repeat (>38 repeats) in androgen receptor gene on X chromosome
other: Electromyography showing chronic denervation and reinnervation
Nerve conduction studies demonstrating mild sensory neuropathy

distinguishingFeatures: Upper motor neuron signs present in ALS but absent in bulbospinal muscular atrophy
No androgen receptor gene mutation in ALS
Lack of gynecomastia and endocrine features

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness with upper motor neuron signs
Severe dysphagia with risk of aspiration pneumonia
references: Kennedy WR, Alter M, Sung JH. Progressive proximal spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy of late onset. A sex-linked recessive trait. Neurology. 1968.
La Spada AR, Wilson EM, Lubahn DB, Harding AE, Fischbeck KH. Androgen receptor gene mutations in X-linked spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy. Nature. 1991.
Rosen DR. The molecular genetics of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Annu Rev Neurosci. 1993.
